# aikido_repository (Resource)

Manages activation and configuration of an existing Aikido code repository.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "aikido_repository" "example" {
  id     = "12345"
  active = true

  sensitivity  = "sensitive"
  connectivity = "connected"

  labels = [
    { name = "payments" },
    { name = "production" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the repository is activated for scanning in Aikido.
- `id` (String) Aikido code repository ID.

### Optional

- `connectivity` (String) Whether the code runs on an internet-connected server. One of: connected, not_connected, unknown.
- `labels` (Attributes List) Labels are managed by this resource. Removing labels from config or setting an empty list deletes them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--labels))
- `sensitivity` (String) Sensitivity level of the repository. One of: extreme, sensitive, normal, not_sensitive, no_data.

### Read-Only

- `branch` (String) Branch configured for scanning.
- `external_repo_id` (String) Repository ID from the Git provider.
- `name` (String) Name of the code repository.
- `git_provider` (String) Git provider hosting the repository (e.g. github, gitlab, bitbucket).
- `url` (String) External URL of the repository.

<a id="nestedatt--labels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `labels`

Required:

- `name` (String) Label name.

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Aikido label ID.
- `is_imported` (Boolean) True when the label was imported from the Git provider (read-only).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import aikido_repository.example 12345
```
